item.research_question: How does copper content affect the microstructure, wear, and corrosion resistance of CoCrCuFeNi high-entropy alloys manufactured by powder metallurgy?
item.material_system: CoCrCuFeNi high-entropy alloys with copper content varying from 0 to 20 at. %
item.processing_route: Powder metallurgy methods: mechanical alloying and hot pressing of element mixtures, with parameters such as rotational speed of jars (694 rpm), duration (30 min), grinding bodies-to-powder weight ratio (15:1), temperature (950 °C), pressure (35 MPa), and isobaric exposure (3 min)
item.test_conditions: Tribological tests with a high-precision tribometer, corrosion resistance tests in 3.5% NaCl solution
key_findings: The solubility limit of copper in CoCrFeNi solid solution is 9 at. %
Doping with copper increases wear resistance by 23% due to solid solution hardening
Wear resistance declines with increasing copper concentration due to segregation of the excess FCC2 phase and decreasing hardness
The wear products are amorphous particles consisting of the alloy components with uniformly distributed oxygen and silicon elements
Formation of the duplex structure FCC1 + FCC2 has a beneficial effect on corrosion resistance compared to the single-phase HEA
Corrosion current density decreases monotonically from 2.24 to 0.4 mA·cm−2 as copper concentration increases from 10 to 20 at. %
item.mechanism: The increase in wear resistance is attributed to solid solution hardening caused by distortion of the crystal lattice of the (Fe)Co,Ni,Cr solid solution, while the decline in wear resistance is due to segregation of the excess FCC2 phase and decreasing hardness
quotes: The solubility limit of copper in CoCrFeNi solid solution was found to be 9 at. %
The wear products were amorphous particles consisting of the alloy components with uniformly distributed oxygen and silicon elements

records.text: Paper card. Question: How does copper content affect the microstructure, wear, and corrosion resistance of CoCrCuFeNi high-entropy alloys manufactured by powder metallurgy?. System: CoCrCuFeNi high-entropy alloys with copper content varying from 0 to 20 at. %. Processing: Powder metallurgy methods: mechanical alloying and hot pressing of element mixtures, with parameters such as rotational speed of jars (694 rpm), duration (30 min), grinding bodies-to-powder weight ratio (15:1), temperature (950 °C), pressure (35 MPa), and isobaric exposure (3 min). Test conditions: Tribological tests with a high-precision tribometer, corrosion resistance tests in 3.5% NaCl solution. Findings: The solubility limit of copper in CoCrFeNi solid solution is 9 at. %; Doping with copper increases wear resistance by 23% due to solid solution hardening; Wear resistance declines with increasing copper concentration due to segregation of the excess FCC2 phase and decreasing hardness; The wear products are amorphous particles consisting of the alloy components with uniformly distributed oxygen and silicon elements; Formation of the duplex structure FCC1 + FCC2 has a beneficial effect on corrosion resistance compared to the single-phase HEA; Corrosion current density decreases monotonically from 2.24 to 0.4 mA·cm−2 as copper concentration increases from 10 to 20 at. %. Mechanism: The increase in wear resistance is attributed to solid solution hardening caused by distortion of the crystal lattice of the (Fe)Co,Ni,Cr solid solution, while the decline in wear resistance is due to segregation of the excess FCC2 phase and decreasing hardness. Quote: "The solubility limit of copper in CoCrFeNi solid solution was found to be 9 at. %"
